### Observed differences

- In the later window, activities A14, A15, A20 and A21 occur much later in the trace: their mean position rises from about 0.32 to about 0.60 of the trace, while A22 and A23 shift slightly earlier (A22 from about 0.35 to 0.32, A23 from about 0.59 to 0.56). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]
- The relative order of these two groups flipped. Before, A14/A15/A20/A21 preceded A22 in about 20–28% of cases and preceded A23 in about 20–28%; after, A22 and A23 precede them in about 22–27% of cases, and the earlier order is no longer observed. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008]
- The outgoing edges of A14, A15, A20 and A21 changed from going to A22 in all observed cases to going to A24 and A28 instead. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- A41, which previously led to A14/A15/A20/A21, now leads to A22 in all observed cases. [DIR008]
- A23 and A24 now also lead to A14/A15/A20/A21, and the gap between A23 and A24/A28 widened (e.g., A23→A28 moved from lag 2 to lag 3). [DIR006, DIR007, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural change in which a group of activities (A14, A15, A20, A21) moved from occurring before A22/A23 to occurring after them, and their outgoing transitions changed from A22 to A24/A28. The number of qualifying items (25) is far above the 0.37 expected by chance, and the relational, positional, lag and successor indicators all point in the same direction. A competing explanation—that the differences reflect sampling variation in variant frequencies—is unlikely given the consistency and volume of the evidence, though the exact mechanism (e.g., whether the group was moved as a block or the edges were rewired) is not fully pinned down.
